Tempos often bogged in '74 and The Wall of Sound tended to record in a flatter, less engaging way, with an undynamic image, but put that aside and there is much of note from this night.

whyThisShow: This show has canonical weight both for its music and its availability — it came out as Dave's Picks Vol. 34, and the Jerry Moore AUD was, as one listener put it, "heavily traded BitD of B&P, and often the lone representative from this tour on tape lists". The second-set sequence is the reason heads keep coming back: one reviewer described the Spanish Jam > U.S. Blues as the moment "the band emerges as one and the music feels like a big truck rolling down a highway out of control, the epitome of '74, yet one-of-a-kind". One reviewer also called out "Phil takes the lead on Spanish Jam and drives the band into the best? version of 1974". One well-sourced listener does caution that the SBD has issues — Bobby's guitar drops out repeatedly — and recommends the matrix or AUD over the SBD/OFF for much of the show.
listenFor: The once-played "Let It Rock" is the rarity flag here — one reviewer couldn't get over why it didn't get more play: "I will never understand. A perfect match for the bebob belooha screech and scratchin that is the first half of the 70's". The "To Lay Me Down" drew attention as "a best-ever candidate" for the solo. One reviewer zeroed in on a specific moment in Cumberland Blues: "listen @5mins when Jer briefly quotes Hank Garland's Sugar Foot Rag". On the source question, the matrix (122270_mtx_tobin) is flagged as "crucial" and the upgraded SBD (122255_upg-sbd_smith-tobin) addresses pitch issues in the original cribbs recording, which "ran 1% fast in many places".
context: June 1974 sits squarely in the Wall of Sound era, when the Dead were road-testing one of the most elaborate live sound systems ever built. This show was played at the Miami Jai-Alai Fronton — an unusual venue — and was officially released as Dave's Picks Vol. 34, making it one of the few Wall of Sound shows to receive a full archival release. The best available recording is a soundboard (gd74-06-23.sbd.cribbs.16780.sbeok.shnf), though the matrix and AUD transfers are widely considered better options for much of the show. One reviewer notes this was also "the first Phil & Ned Seastones" of the tour, a detail that places it as a minor historical marker within the summer '74 run.
funFact: "Let it Rock" was only played once by the Dead, and one listener traces why the band even knew it: "the original Berry single was a Brit hit (not stateside)" and Jerry had been playing it in Garcia & Saunders sets.
headline: Miami '74, with the one-time Let It Rock.
